relationships.subject: AM-2099
relationships.evidence_quote: Inhibition of Nav1.7 channels by 600 nM AM-2099 generally produced a substantial depolarizing shift of action potential threshold, an increase in rheobase, a decrease in action potential upstroke velocity, decrease in action potential peak, and prolongation of refractory period.

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: Nav1.8 inhibition produced much more dramatic reduction of repetitive firing than Nav1.7 inhibition.

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: In contrast, a selective Nav1.8 channel inhibitor (suzetrigine) has had successful clinical trials.

key_findings: Nav1.7 inhibition with AM-2099 shifts action potential threshold and refractory period in human DRG neurons more than Nav1.8 inhibition.
Repetitive firing with strong stimuli is little affected by Nav1.7 inhibition, unlike Nav1.8 inhibition.
